result:
Staging through the New-Project Entry, with the spec's R1–R11 as outcome candidates. Before I write any roadmap text, I need your ranking and a check on the tracks.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index catalog in Parquet for a quarter range you choose, built from the SEC's archived quarterly indexes | R1, R3 | About 20–50 MB per recent quarter's `master.idx`, so a few GB for a 1993-to-now range. Basis: roughly 300–400k rows × ~100 bytes. This is arithmetic I have not checked against the listing. Request count is trivial at 3 req/s (one file per quarter), so bandwidth and parse time dominate. |
| O2 | The catalog extended with each day's new filings, catching up after missed days and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 small files a year. Negligible. |
| O3 | Re-running the parser over stored original files without downloading anything again | R6 | Storage only: raw bytes kept, roughly the size of O1 plus O2. |
| O4 | Weekly re-reads of quarterly indexes, with additions and changed fields recorded against the catalog | R7 | One full re-download of every supported quarter per run, so O1's volume each week. Your chosen range drives this. |
| O5 | Records that disappear from a closed quarter stay in the catalog until you approve that exact replacement | R10 | Mostly your time per approval. Frequency is unknown until reconciliation runs on real data. |
| O6 | Readers get each quarter's complete current version through one pointer, never half-written files | R9 | Small; not material. |
| O7 | Every run shares one SEC request budget, so adding workers never adds SEC traffic | R8 | Not material in compute. It matters once more than one runner exists. |
| O8 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs scheduled and monitored on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor), with alerts and runbooks | R4, §4.7, §4.9 | Azure spend can't be estimated until it runs. That track's core stage measures it. |

R5 (one shared downloader, parser and publisher) and R11 (the §4.8 defaults are starting values) describe how to build it, not what you get. I've recorded them as choices below instead of listing them as outcomes.

## Tracks

- **Track A — Catalog (O1–O7), known progression.** The spec's §7 already names the order: baseline, daily, replay, reconciliation, withdrawal gate.
- **Track B — Azure operation (O8), known progression.** I split this from A because the catalog can be built and checked against real SEC files on any machine. Joining the tracks would make the first usable catalog wait on ADF, Container Apps Jobs and identity setup. O7 sits in A, but its cross-machine form (the Storage-backed lease) only matters once B exists.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, as a uv workspace (`.python-version`, root `pyproject.toml`).
- Shared code across backfill, daily and reconciliation (R5).
- §4.8 values are starting defaults that change only through configuration review (R11).
- Azure stack per the ADR. Note that the ADR and the spec are both still **Proposed**, not accepted.

## Proposed name

`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The skill takes the spec's own filename stem whole.

## One request

Please rank the outcomes within Track A, then rank the two tracks against each other. Also confirm or change the split, the kinds and the name.

Optionally, I can firm up O1's cost by fetching one real quarter's `index.json` listing and `master.idx` to get an actual size. That needs the SEC User-Agent identity you want to use (organization or name, plus a contact email). I'll only run it if you say yes.
